Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for sudden-onset left-sided headache with visual disturbance, dizziness, nausea, and vomiting in a woman with minimal past history.
- Clinical impression: probable migraine. Advised OTC therapy (ibuprofen + anti-sickness) and arranged same-day in-person neurological assessment; may cancel if symptoms resolve.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute unilateral headache with visual symptoms — probable migraine
  - Onset/duration: Began this morning; ~4 hours before consult; abrupt onset.
  - Character/location: Left-sided headache; not clearly behind the eye; intensity ~6/10.
  - Associated symptoms: Blurred vision with zigzag lines, dizziness, nausea, vomiting x2, worsened by movement; difficulty tolerating screens.
  - Pertinent negatives: No limb weakness; able to walk in a straight line; no prior similar headaches.
  - Medications tried: Acetaminophen (paracetamol) taken ~3 hours after onset; no relief.
  - Family history: Mother with migraines; hypothyroidism in family.
  - Examination: No in-person exam performed during telehealth; patient-reported no focal deficits.
  - Clinical impression: Migraine with visual aura considered likely.
  - Plan: Trial ibuprofen plus anti-sickness medication (from pharmacy) and a sugary carbonated drink; arrange same-day in-person neurological exam; consider escalation to specific migraine medications if inadequate response; may cancel appointment if markedly improved before the visit; contact clinic if any further problems prior to appointment.

Issue 2:
- Health anxiety related to headache
  - Patient expressed concern about serious causes (tumor, stroke).
  - Reassurance provided regarding likely migraine features; safety plan as above with prompt in-person assessment.

Issue 3:
- History of kidney stones
  - Past episode noted; no active issues discussed today.

Medications:
- Acetaminophen (paracetamol) — dose/route/frequency not documented; taken ~3 hours after onset; ineffective.
- Ibuprofen — recommended; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Anti-sickness medication — recommended (pharmacy); specific agent/dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies (per patient).

Past Medical History:
- Kidney stones (previous history; date not specified).
- Family history: Migraines (mother); hypothyroidism in family.

Social History:
- Not documented.

Preventative History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Exam: Telehealth only; no physical/neuro exam performed. Patient reports no focal weakness and normal gait.

Plan:
- Start ibuprofen with an anti-sickness medication (pharmacy advice); add a sugary carbonated drink as discussed.
- Same-day in-person appointment arranged for full neurological examination; if symptoms significantly improve before the appointment, patient may call to cancel.
- If medications do not help or symptoms persist/worsen before the appointment, contact the clinic; further evaluation may include specific migraine therapies.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; full neurological exam; detailed review of systems (fever/neck stiffness/photophobia explicitly); pregnancy status not confirmed by test; medication doses/routes/frequencies; comprehensive medication and allergy reconciliation; social history (smoking/alcohol); preventive care status.
- Internal conflicts: Doctor briefly repeated “hyperthyroid,” but patient clarified family history is hypothyroidism (conflict noted). Patient initially answered “Yes” to other medical problems, then said “not actually” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Minor connectivity issues and brief repetitions; overall content understandable.
